title: What is the angle between two spokes of the wheel?
description: Twenty four equal gaps fill a full turn of three hundred sixty degrees, so one gap is fifteen degrees. Two spokes that are some gaps apart make that many fifteens, and the largest one under ninety is seventy five degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal gaps share the full turn, and an angle between any two spokes is a count of gaps times the gap angle. Watch for students who count ninety degrees as acute.

video_script.why: The child shares the full turn equally among the gaps, and then counts gaps to find the largest angle under ninety.
video_script.substitution: 360 divided by 24 gives 15; counting 1 to 6 gaps gives 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90; the last one under 90 is 75.
video_script.payoff_line: Share the full turn equally, and then count the gaps

final_answer.value: 15° between neighbouring spokes; the largest acute angle is 75°
final_answer.spoken: the angle between neighbouring spokes is fifteen degrees, and the largest acute angle between two spokes is seventy five degrees

names.{{NAME_4}}: the wheel with equal spokes on the national flag

never_show: ninety degrees named as an acute angle
maths_rules: two spokes k gaps apart make k × 15°
acute: less than 90°, so k × 15 < 90, so k is at most 5
video_script.design: One wheel. A single gap is shaded teal, then gaps are counted off from one spoke; five gaps are amber and the sixth turns grey as a right angle.

<bookmark mark='more'/>Five gaps make seventy five, and six gaps make ninety.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Fifteen, thirty, forty five, sixty, seventy five, ninety.

<bookmark mark='out'/>Ninety is a right angle, so it is out.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last angle in the row under ninety is the largest acute angle.
